faqs.q: How much does a Dogue de Bordeaux cost to buy?
faqs.a: Reputable breeders typically charge $1,200–$4,000 for a Dogue de Bordeaux puppy. Prices vary by breeder reputation, health testing, and lineage. Rescue adoption fees are typically $100–$500 and include vaccinations, neutering, and microchipping.

faqs.q: What is the monthly cost of owning a Dogue de Bordeaux?
faqs.a: Budget $200–$400 per month for a Dogue de Bordeaux, covering food, preventive vet care, insurance, grooming and supplies. Large breeds cost more across every category — food portions, medication doses and professional services all scale with weight.

faqs.q: What are the biggest ongoing costs for a Dogue de Bordeaux?
faqs.a: The three largest annual expenses are food ($800–1,200), veterinary care ($400–$1,200 budgeted annually), and pet insurance ($800–1,800 per year). Grooming adds $400–$1,200 annually for Dogue de Bordeauxs due to their coat type.

faqs.q: How much does a Dogue de Bordeaux cost in the first year?
faqs.a: Year one costs for a Dogue de Bordeaux are significantly higher than subsequent years, typically $2,500–$5,000. This covers the purchase price or adoption fee, initial vet checks, vaccinations, spay/neuter, microchipping, crate, bedding, collar, leads and puppy training classes.

faqs.q: How often should I groom a Dogue de Bordeaux?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs need brushing 3–5 times per week, daily during seasonal coat blows.  Nails should be trimmed every 3–4 weeks. Ears should be checked and cleaned monthly.

faqs.q: Do Dogue de Bordeauxs shed a lot?
faqs.a: Yes — they are considered heavy shedders. Regular brushing is the most effective control tool. A slicker brush and undercoat rake are both essential for Dogue de Bordeauxs. Deshedding treatments from professional groomers can reduce seasonal shedding temporarily.

faqs.q: What grooming tools does a Dogue de Bordeaux need?
faqs.a: A slicker brush for surface debris and an undercoat rake for the dense undercoat are both essential. A shedding blade or deshedding tool helps during heavy moult periods. A nail grinder is useful if your Dogue de Bordeaux is sensitive to clippers.

faqs.q: How often should I bathe a Dogue de Bordeaux?
faqs.a: Every 4–6 weeks is appropriate for most Dogue de Bordeauxs that live indoors. More frequent bathing is needed if they swim or spend time in mud. Over-bathing strips natural skin oils — use a pH-balanced dog shampoo rather than human products.

faqs.q: Are Dogue de Bordeauxs easy to train?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs are considered easier to train than average — they respond quickly to reward-based methods and generalise cues well. Short 10–15 minute sessions outperform long correction-heavy drills.

faqs.q: What training method works best for a Dogue de Bordeaux?
faqs.a: Reward-based training using treats, praise and toy rewards is the most effective and well-researched approach for Dogue de Bordeauxs. Keep sessions short and positive, end on a success, and vary your rewards to maintain engagement.

faqs.q: At what age should I start training my Dogue de Bordeaux?
faqs.a: Start training from the day your puppy arrives home, typically at 8 weeks. The 8–16 week window is the most sensitive socialisation period. Enrol in a puppy class within the first two weeks for structured socialisation alongside basic obedience foundations.

faqs.q: How long does it take to train a Dogue de Bordeaux?
faqs.a: Most Dogue de Bordeauxs learn basic obedience cues (sit, stay, come, down) within 2–4 weeks of daily practice. Reliable recall in distracting environments typically takes 2–3 months of consistent reinforcement.

faqs.q: What health problems do Dogue de Bordeauxs commonly have?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs are most commonly associated with bloat (GDV). Regular vet checks, appropriate weight management, and breed-specific screening tests help detect issues early. Ask any breeder for health test results before purchasing.

faqs.q: How long do Dogue de Bordeauxs live?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs have an average lifespan of 5–8 years. Larger breeds typically have shorter lifespans than smaller breeds. Maintaining a healthy weight and regular vet care are the most impactful factors for longevity.

faqs.q: Are Dogue de Bordeauxs prone to hip dysplasia?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs have a moderate-to-elevated risk of hip dysplasia, particularly for large or active breeds. Ask for OFA or PennHIP hip evaluation certificates when buying from a breeder. Weight control and avoiding high-impact exercise during bone growth (under 18 months) reduces risk.

faqs.q: What health tests should a Dogue de Bordeaux puppy have?
faqs.a: At minimum, your Dogue de Bordeaux puppy should have a vet health check, first vaccinations, deworming, and microchipping before coming home. Ask the breeder for parent health certificates relevant to Dogue de Bordeaux-specific conditions. A vet check within 72 hours of bringing your puppy home is recommended to establish a baseline.

faqs.q: Are Dogue de Bordeauxs good with kids?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs are generally known for being friendly and patient, making them well-suited to family life with children. Supervision is always recommended with young children regardless of breed — interactions should be taught from both sides.

faqs.q: Do Dogue de Bordeauxs get along with other dogs?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs are generally sociable with other dogs, particularly when well-socialised from puppyhood. Introduce new dogs on neutral territory and keep initial meetings brief and positive.

faqs.q: Do Dogue de Bordeauxs bark a lot?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs are not considered excessive barkers. They may alert to strangers or unusual sounds, but are generally manageable with basic training. Consistent "quiet" reinforcement from puppyhood keeps this in check.

faqs.q: Are Dogue de Bordeauxs good apartment dogs?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs can live in apartments if their exercise needs are met consistently. The key variable is owner commitment to daily walks and enrichment — breed size alone doesn't determine apartment suitability.

faqs.q: How much exercise does a Dogue de Bordeaux need per day?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs need approximately 45–60 minutes of exercise daily. A structured morning walk and an evening sniff walk usually cover their needs. Mental exercise (training sessions, puzzle feeders) counts toward overall stimulation needs and can reduce restless behaviour.

faqs.q: Are Dogue de Bordeauxs good running partners?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs can join you for moderate runs once fully grown. They're better suited to steady 3–5 mile runs than extended distance. Watch for signs of fatigue and always run in cooler hours during summer.

faqs.q: What happens if a Dogue de Bordeaux doesn't get enough exercise?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs are less demanding than high-energy breeds, but chronic under-exercise still leads to weight gain and low-level restlessness. Even lower-energy breeds benefit from a consistent daily walk for both physical health and mental stimulation.

faqs.q: Can a Dogue de Bordeaux be off-lead?
faqs.a: Off-lead freedom for a Dogue de Bordeaux depends on recall reliability, not breed alone. Train recall from puppyhood using long-line sessions before progressing to full off-lead. A standard 20-foot long-line gives freedom while maintaining safety during the training phase.

faqs.q: How much should I feed my Dogue de Bordeaux?
faqs.a: A Dogue de Bordeaux needs approximately 3–5 cups of dry food per day for an adult, split across two meals. Always follow the feeding guide on your specific formula — calorie density varies significantly between brands. Adjust portions based on body condition: you should be able to feel (but not easily see) the ribs.

faqs.q: How many times a day should I feed a Dogue de Bordeaux?
faqs.a: Adult Dogue de Bordeauxs should eat twice daily. Puppies (under 6 months) need 3–4 smaller meals per day to support growth and prevent hypoglycaemia, particularly in small breeds. For large and giant breeds, twice daily feeding also reduces the risk of bloat (GDV) compared to one large daily meal.

faqs.q: What is the best food for a Dogue de Bordeaux?
faqs.a: Look for a formula carrying an AAFCO adequacy statement for the correct life stage. A named protein source (chicken, turkey, beef, salmon) should appear first in the ingredient list. Medium-energy Dogue de Bordeauxs do well on standard adult maintenance formulas with named protein as the first ingredient.

faqs.q: When should I switch my Dogue de Bordeaux from puppy to adult food?
faqs.a: Large breeds should stay on a large-breed puppy formula until 18–24 months, then transition to an adult formula. Switching too early can disrupt joint development during the growth phase.

faqs.q: Is a Dogue de Bordeaux a good dog for first-time owners?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs are manageable for motivated first-time owners who research the breed, commit to early training, and have realistic expectations about time and cost.

faqs.q: Are Dogue de Bordeauxs good family dogs?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs are typically affectionate family dogs that do well with children and adapt to household routines. Their sociable nature means they prefer company over isolation.

faqs.q: Do Dogue de Bordeauxs do well when left alone?
faqs.a: Dogue de Bordeauxs form strong bonds with their owners and do not do well with extended isolation. Aim for no more than 4–6 hours alone at a time. If your schedule requires longer absences, consider a dog walker, doggy daycare, or a companion dog.

faqs.q: How much time do you need for a Dogue de Bordeaux?
faqs.a: Plan for 1.5–2 hours per day dedicated to your Dogue de Bordeaux — covering exercise, training, feeding and general interaction. Add 15–30 minutes for grooming 3–4 times weekly. The commitment is consistent year-round, not just when convenient.
